en: Thanks for the ride... Oh, right, the fare.
(He looks even gloomier now.)
(Guess encouraging young people isn't as easy as I thought.)
I'm from Nagasu Taxi. Sorry for the wait.
To the airport, please.
(Has she been crying? Her eyes are all puffy. Maybe she's going through a tough time.)
Of course. Let's go.
(It looks like she's upset about something. I'll see if I can strike up a conversation.)
You'll get carsick if you stare out the window.
Mind your own business, won't you? I'm having a hard time and I just wanted to look at the scenery.
I see Hakata has a special place in your heart.
That's a very astute observation.
You were just staring out with such fondness.
Yes. This is where I was born and raised. I have so many unforgettable memories here.
I never thought I'd end up leaving.
Oh? Why are you leaving?
I'm to be married to a man in Tokyo. I'm off to go live with him there.
He's from a good family, and quite wealthy.
...You really don't know how to read people, do you?
I wanted to talk to someone about it, but I doubt you'd understand.
Oh. Sorry.
*sigh* Never mind.
You don't look too happy about it.
Hm? Ha. Well, no.
You're quite perceptive, aren't you?
I was actually seeing a guy here in Hakata for many years. We were in love.
He's a writer, with hopes of being a novelist one day. We were planning to get married once he won that literary prize.
But I couldn't wait for that.
What does he think about you getting married now?
I couldn't bring myself to tell him. I left without saying a word.
Do you think he'll ever be able to forgive me? I think he will, in time. Right?
I'm sure he'll forgive you.
Thank you. That makes me feel a little better about this.
Has something like this ever happened to you?
Well, no.
Then how do you know he'll get over it?
So you just said the first thing you thought of?
No, it's not like that.
Hmph. I feel stupid baring my soul to a taxi driver, of all people. Ugh. Now I just feel worse.
I doubt he'll ever get over it.
What? You make me sound like a woman who's throwing away love for the sake of money!
It wasn't easy of me to make this decision, you know! You have no idea how I feel!
Ugh, never mind! There's no point telling you about it.
There's still time to turn back and tell him.
Oh, I couldn't bear to see the look on his face.
Forgive me for saying this, but are you trying to spare his feelings or yours?
Look, I have no idea if you're making the right call in going off to get married.
But I do think if you run away without saying a word to him, you'll only end up regretting it in the end.
And I can't see that as being good for either of you.
Well, what're you going to do? We're almost at the on-ramp.
...Can I ask you to turn back? I think I'll wait another day to go to Tokyo.
I really must thank you.
If I'd gone to Tokyo today, I would have had to live with that regret the rest of my life.
I have to tell him, face to face. Thank you for helping me realize that.
Here is my fare. Will you accept a tip, too?
Good luck on the rest of your travels!
Thank you. Here's my fare.
Best of luck to you.
I have a feeling this job doesn't suit you.
I apologize.
Yeah. Try putting more thought into what you say next time. Bye.
To <Color:22>Meisei Street<Color:Default> please. There's no hurry, so drive carefully, won't you?
Thank you, driver. Can I ask your name?
It's Suzuki.
Ah. Well, that was a very smooth ride, Suzuki-san. I'll ask for you by name next time.
Be seeing you, then!
You're welcome.
You need to get your act together. You're supposed to be a professional, aren't you?
Well, just try to do better.
(That passenger didn't look too happy. I'll have to be more careful in the future.)
You got 600 experience points.
<Color:22>Fukuhaku Street<Color:Default>, please. I'm in a bit of a rush, but you should make it there in time driving normally, so no need to go crazy fast.
Understood. Let's go.
Wow. We made it on time, and it was a very pleasant ride.
I hope you enjoy your daughter's performance.
I will. Thank you.
I appreciate your help.
It was a pleasure driving you.
Gah! My daughter's going to be so mad at me.
Ah, well. I'll just ask someone else to drive me to next month's recital.
(I really let him down. I'll have to do better in the future.)
Nice day out, huh?
Sure's been awful cold out lately. Every year the fall gets shorter and the winter gets longer, am I right?
Don't you think so, driver?
I guess.
You're pretty quiet for a cabbie.
Hey, driver. There's only so much silence I can take. How long've you been at this job?
Only around six months.
Oh, okay. That explains it.
(What's he talking about?)
Let me put it to you like this.
I don't know about other parts, but here in Fukuoka, taxi drivers are expected to keep up the conversation.
Most of us locals here in Fukuoka like to chat. If you don't have the gift of gab, you're not gonna get any regular customers.
I see... My boss told me the same thing, come to think of it.
I bet he did. Taxi driving's a service job, and small talk's a big part of the service.
Right, but I don't know what to talk about...
Then how about I give you some pointers?
Such as?
Well, I thought we'd do some practice dialogue, help get you started. I'm not speaking the Hakata dialect, so it should be easy to follow. Sound good?
So, how's business today?
I'm asking you, driver.
Oh, sorry. Let's see...
Business is pretty good. It helps when I get passengers like you who are going on longer trips.
There you go. That's how it's done.
Okay. I think I'm getting the hang of this.
Business could be better. Long-distance fares like these mean my cab's going to be empty on the return trip.
Come on, why would you bring that up? You gotta make the customer feel welcome, even if you don't mean it.
Oh... Then that's tricky.
None of your damn business.
Whoa! Where'd that come from?
Oh, sorry. The line sounded cool in my head, so I thought it'd be appropriate.
Come on, what did we just talk about? The goal here is to get a conversation going!
Right, conversation...
So why'd you go off spouting some random one-liner? You trying to be a comedian?
No, not really...
Look, don't overthink it. All you have to do is think of something casual and inoffensive to say. There's nothing complicated about this.
So, have you gotten the hang of the job yet?
No, I still have plenty to learn.
Yeah, I imagine it takes time.
What sort of work do you do?
Me? I'm more of a glorified security guard than anything... Never mind that, though. Different subject.
What's your favorite Hakata food so far?
Well, I tried mizutaki the other day, and it was delicious.
Yeah, it's pretty tasty, isn't it? Goes well with sake, so it's perfect for those who like their drink. You a big drinker?
Oh, I'll have a drink every now and then.
I'd have to say Hakata ramen.
Ah, Hakata ramen's a classic. Each restaurant has its own take on the standard tonkotsu broth. You should try out as many different places as you can.
I might just do that.
Do you even need to ask? It's gotta be takoyaki.

Hey, takoyaki's a Kansai thing! Don't get us confused.
And what's with the attitude all of a sudden?
Sorry. I don't know what came over me...
You're a strange one, aren't you...
Oh, hey, you know what you should try next? <Italic>Gameni.</Italic>
Gameni...? Never heard of that one. Is it any good?

Why sure. You might hear some people call it <Italic>chikuzenni</Italic>.
Anyway, it's a chicken and vegetable stew.
We always have it at New Year's⑬
The car behind us sped up all of a sudden and tried to run us off the road. Are you all right, sir?
I'm fine. But that car... It looks like they're one of the <Color:7>Devil Killers<Color:Default>!
<Color:7>Devil Killers<Color:Default>?
Street racers who cause nothing but trouble.
They challenge people on the road and shake them down for money if they lose. Happened to a lot of people already.
(That punk from earlier said he was with the Devil Killers, now that I think back on it. I didn't realize they were this much of a menace.)
Now they've decided to pick on a local taxi? Bunch of goddamn lunatics...
You know what, though. A professional driver like you should be more than capable of handling them. Go ahead and take them on.
I don't know if that's a good idea...
I didn't tell you, but I'm actually with the motor patrol unit of the Fukuoka Police.
What? You're an officer?

Yeah, and not the kind who sits back on his ass while
a bunch of little shits pretend like they own the road.

Driver, you have my permission. We need to take a stand
against these reckless criminals if we want to keep the
streets safe for our citizens!

I can't guarantee this will turn out how you want...
but I might as well give it a shot.
Great! Let's burn some rubber!
Here goes nothing.
What's the job?
It's the foreigner from the other day again. You know, DeVille something-or-other.
(Must be Watanabe of the Devil Killers again. This time I'll win, no matter what.)
I'll be heading out, then.
Well, it's a pickup request, but I find it rather strange.
Oh, just... Calling a taxi to pick you up from a highway rest area seems rather odd, don't you think?
For instance, that's where those rowdy packs of motorheads are always hanging out. Please be careful out there.
(This is probably a challenge from the Devil Killers. I better keep my promise to Furumichi.)
If you're going to face off with the Devil Killers, I suggest you think better of it.
Well, it's only dumb luck that a regular old driver like you managed to win. And that was one time.
You let your ego run wild and you'll get in over your head. These guys don't mess around.
I appreciate your concern. But this is something I have to do for everyone's benefit, including yours.
Muramatsu-kun?
Is this "DeVille Kellars" a foreigner or something? Everyone seems to be talking about him lately.
Run him into the ground, Aniki!
Heh, don't you worry. You're about to see this loser get left in the dust... again! Can't wait to see the look on his face!
Quit running your mouth and get behind the wheel.
Been waitin' for you, taxi man!

I'm surprised you didn't turn tail and run, considering how
badly you lost the other day.
Hah! It ain't me you're up against.
I got my aniki here to step up for me! And he's the roughest, toughest Devil Killer you ever saw! Tell him, Aniki!
So you're the cabbie who did a number on Nagata, huh?
What if I am? You here to avenge him?
He sure is! Our aniki here, he would never let⑬
Shut up. This ain't about you, dumbass.
It's not!? Then why...
I'm pissed that one of the mighty Devil Killers lost to some nobody who carts around passengers for a living!
If the Four Kings got word of this, they'd blow a gasket.
The Four Kings?
Forget that shit! All you need to know is you're about to get beat to a pulp, all for the glory of the Devil Killers!
You rock, Aniki!
Hahaha! Whaddya expect? It's just a fuckin' taxi driver!
What? You all sad now!? Don't worry, you can swallow my fumes again any day you want. I'll leave ya chokin' on my exhaust pipe!
Hahahaha! Ahhh... I love being aniki sometimes.
Nah, this can't be real... I'm a Devil Killer and he's⑬ he's just a cab driver!
What happened, Aniki!? If the Four Kings find out about this, we're done for!
...Even so. We gotta tell 'em.
But you can't! We'd be in deep shit for runnin' the Devil Killers' name into the ground!
You little turd! Stop thinkin' of yourself over the honor of the team! We can't let this defeat stand!
Yo. The Four Kings'll give you a personal demo of why no one messes with us. You'll see!
Who are these Four Kings you keep talking about?
You'll find out soon enough. You'll wish you never crossed paths with <Italic>real</Italic> hardcore street racers like us!
(Looks like bringing down the Devil Killers is going to take a lot longer than I thought...)
Oh, hi there, Suzuki-san. Did you get along okay with that DeVille fellow?
I did. He might even be a regular customer now.
Excellent to hear.
Well? What happened?
Nothing much. I did win a race, though.
Wait, you beat the Devil Killers <Italic>again</Italic>!? I don't believe what I'm hearing...
Muramatsu-san, could it be you're familiar with the street racing scene?
No, that would be crazy... I just don't think you should be going around racing on public roads like that.
